newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call extra EU summit on May 23.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call extra EU summit on May 23.

text.p: EU heads of government will meet at an informal summit in the Dutch coastal town of Noordwijk on May 23, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Friday.

The Netherlands, which currently holds the European Union presidency, called the extra session to give impetus to the inter-governmental conference (IGC) on EU reforms ahead of an Amsterdam summit on June 16-17.

The IGC, a ministerial review of the EU's "constitution", aims to produce a more efficient and transparent Union, paving the way for an ambitious eastward expansion that could see up to a dozen ex-communist states joining in the next decade.

Just six weeks before EU leaders are due to sign landmark treaty reforms at Amsterdam, negotiations are bogged down over how to change EU institutions -- the size of a future European Commission, the EU's executive arm, and how to ensure the decision-making process fairly represents each country's population.
The extra summit will also give member states the chance to quiz Britain's new Prime Minister Tony Blair on his stance towards deeper EU integration as planned under the IGC.
Blair's Labour Party, which won a resounding victory in Thursday's general election, is widely seen as more cooperative towards Europe than the defeated Conservatives.
